userAction: The user reported freezing and closure while trying to open the menu.

confirmed.failedWorkaround: This is the same PID started at14:38:40 with -gpu swiftshader -feature -Vulkan. Disabling Vulkan did not prevent recurrence.
confirmed.dumpCorrection: The first investigation checked WER and the emulator crash database but missed Windows LocalAppData/CrashDumps. Usable dumps for both visible and two earlier headless crashes exist there.

dumpAnalysis.method: Read-only parsing of MINIDUMP exception/context, thread, module and memory streams; raw stack module matches and call-site byte checks, not symbolic stack unwinding.
dumpAnalysis.matchingInstruction: Both visible crashes execute identical MOVDQU xmm0,[rbp+r9+0x184e0] bytes, f3 42 0f 6f 84 0d e0 84 01 00. The calculated 16-byte read address matches the exception data address in both.
dumpAnalysis.sharedCallSites: Both visible dumps have candidate return addresses in SwiftShader libGLESv2.dll at +0x207aba,+0x207eb9,+0x207fbf,+0x208340,+0x208381,+0x182647. PE bytes confirm calls immediately before those addresses. Earlier headless dumps share the worker path.
dumpAnalysis.scope: Evidence strongly implicates the SwiftShader GLES rendering path. The exact generated shader/buffer defect is not established without symbols/unwinding. Vulkan-off still used SwiftShader GLES.

confirmed.androidEvidence: After reboot, latest persisted NEXTV exit-info remains the .71 PACKAGE UPDATED event. Current-boot crash buffer is empty. Abrupt VM death may prevent guest records from persisting.
